queue.title: Managing Labor Disputes: Escalation Prevention
queue.content:
A labor dispute reaching court could almost always have been resolved earlier, more cheaply. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A labor dispute that reaches court could almost always have been resolved more cheaply at an earlier stage, with a clear internal procedure.

A labor dispute that reaches court could almost always have been resolved more cheaply at an earlier stage, with a clear internal procedure.

Employee dissatisfaction not addressed through a clear internal grievance channel often escalates into a formal dispute that is both costlier and more prolonged than early, direct resolution.

A documented, consistently applied internal grievance process — with clear deadlines and a named responsible person — reduces the likelihood a dispute escalates beyond the company at all.

Inconsistent application of internal rules to different employees in similar situations creates grounds for legal dispute regardless of whether the underlying decision was justified.

Regular management training on proper handling of grievances and disciplinary measures reduces procedural errors that can lose a dispute on their own, regardless of the merits.

queue.title: Valuing Intangible Assets in Acquisitions
queue.content:
Intangible assets often make up more of an acquisition price than tangible ones, yet are harder to value. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

In an acquisition, intangible assets like brand and customer base often make up a larger share of the price than tangible assets.

In an acquisition, intangible assets like brand and customer base often make up a larger share of the price than tangible assets, yet are harder to value objectively.

In modern acquisitions, especially in tech and services, intangible assets — brand, customer relationships, proprietary technology — often exceed the value of tangible assets on the balance sheet.

Intangible-asset valuation methods (cost, market, income) yield different results, so transparency about the chosen method is key to both sides' trust in negotiations.

Overvaluing intangible assets to justify a higher purchase price creates a risk of subsequent impairment on the buyer's balance sheet, with a direct impact on future financial statements.

An independent valuation of intangible assets, conducted before final price negotiations, reduces room for later dispute over whether the price paid was justified.

queue.title: Technology Integration Speed Does Not Replace Testing
queue.content:
A system launched before thorough testing usually gets tested live, at customers' expense. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

A system launched before it has been thoroughly tested usually ends up tested live, at the expense of customers who never asked for that.

A system launched before it has been thoroughly tested usually ends up tested live, at the expense of customers who never asked for that.

The pressure to deploy new technology ahead of competitors often shortens testing precisely when it should be most thorough, since the cost of a production error always exceeds the cost of a delayed launch. GNK ASG d.o.o. separates the innovation phase from the production-stability phase precisely because of that difference in risk.

Separating the experimentation phase from the production-stability phase lets innovation move fast while keeping the risk of error confined to a controlled environment.

This commentary is part of the GNK ASG Intelligence Desk system and is informational in nature.
